mechanism_narrative: A collapse in transit station mobility removes the foot-traffic pipeline for discretionary retail, so RETAIL_REC continues to fall over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from 0.9 to -21.3 between t-3w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days while TRANSIT remains below -20 in the first week after the decision point.

mechanism_narrative: Workplace mobility below -10 signals enforceable stay-at-home or workplace-closure orders, which suppress weekday retail traffic and drive RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES dropped from 0.3 to -16.9 over four weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES remains below -10 but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: When both transit and workplace mobility fall sharply together, the combined loss of commuting and leisure trips amplifies the retail decline more than either series alone, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both fell by more than 15 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall more than 15 points, RETAIL_REC does not decline further over the next 4 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility above +4 indicates broad voluntary or mandated staying at home, which directly reduces trips to retail and recreation venues and lowers RETAIL_REC over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 1.0 to 5.9 between t-3w and t-0w
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL above +4 is followed by a RETAIL_REC mean over the next 7 days that is higher than the last 7-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in grocery and pharmacy mobility signals that even essential errands are being curtailed, predicting a broader consumer retrenchment that keeps RETAIL_REC depressed over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from 0.6 to -13.4 over four weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM remains below -10 but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The joint regime of workplace closures and elevated residential mobility creates a shutdown feedback loop: fewer work trips and more home time jointly depress retail footfall over four weeks.
failure_condition: The joint condition holds but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is at least as high as the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Early spring normally lifts park visits and outdoor retail, but the current park mobility collapse signals that pandemic fears override seasonal demand, keeping RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 8.0 to -11.1 between t-3w and t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS remains below -10 but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The one-week plunge in retail and transit mobility is an overreaction that will mean-revert as consumers adapt to restrictions, causing RETAIL_REC to average higher over the next four weeks than the last four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC at -17.7 and TRANSIT at -21.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below -15 for at least two of the next four weeks and the next 28-day mean is lower than the last 28-day mean.
